brief: An ornate carved oak library table, 1.2 m long, 75 cm deep and 76 cm high. Its thick top has a moulded edge, an ovolo over a small cove. Its frieze is carved in relief with a ten-petalled rosette at the middle of each long side and a running scroll of acanthus leaves out from it to each end. It stands on four turned baluster legs: a bun foot, a gadrooned bulb, a neck wrapped in acanthus leaves, a fluted column and a collar under a square block, braced low by an H-shaped stretcher of turned rails. Old oak, hand-waxed and darkened with age, its edges and the proudest leaves rubbed paler by hands, dust and old wax dark in the carving's hollows. Made by hand two hundred years ago.
